slides.title: Stated intent overstates Copilot demand: three times as many admins said they would buy as beta accounts paid

claims.claim: 46% of survey respondents said they were likely to buy at $149; 14% of beta accounts actually paid
evidence: Survey: likely or very likely 0.46; Paywall test: bought 0.14
Survey: October 2026, 610 of 9,800 admins replied (6%). Paywall test: 120 beta accounts offered Copilot at $149 after the free period; 17 bought

claims.claim: Both samples are larger accounts than the typical customer, so even 14% flatters the base
evidence: Average office seats per account: Survey respondents 9.4; Beta accounts 8.1; All accounts 6.2

claims.claim: Even the paywall rate is a ceiling: volunteers who chose to try Copilot are the likeliest buyers Brightwork has

slides.title: Applied to every account, the paywall rate supports at most $2.5M of add-on ARR, under a third of the $8M case

claims.claim: The $8M rests on what admins said, not on what they paid
evidence: New ARR, first year: Survey case (46% likely to buy) 8; Paywall rate (14% bought) 2.4531
Survey case: 46% × 9,800 accounts × $1,788 a year gives $8.1M, from a 6% response skewed to large accounts
$8M is the CPO's figure from the October 2026 survey; recomputed, 46% of 9,800 accounts at $1,788 a year is $8.06M

claims.claim: Paywall rate: 1,372 buying accounts at most, because the beta converted its keenest volunteers
evidence: 9,800 customer accounts today × 14% bought at $149 in the beta paywall test × $1,788 a year per buyer ($149 × 12) = $2.5M new ARR, a ceiling for the base

claims.claim: Before costs: buyers at 6,800 requests a month would cost about $1.0M a year in inference, plus $0.6M of platform cost

slides.title: The beta's encouraging gains come from volunteers and a few heavy users, not yet from typical accounts

claims.claim: 9 pp faster growth in jobs per dispatcher-hour than matched accounts
evidence: +11% for beta accounts compared with +2% for matched accounts
Dispatchers self-report saving 4.1 hours a week
Volunteers were already more active, so part of the gap is selection
Untested on typical 6.2-seat accounts
Dispatch Copilot beta results, 240 volunteer accounts, 12 weeks, 2026

claims.claim: 4 pp higher 90-day renewal than matched accounts
evidence: 97% for beta accounts compared with 93% for matched accounts
Keen, engaged accounts renew more anyway
A 90-day window says little about annual churn of 14%
Needs a randomised test before it enters the plan

claims.claim: Value and cost both sit with a few heavy users
evidence: 58% of all AI requests came from the top 10% of beta accounts
The median account sends 1,900 requests a month, the top tenth 14,500
Pricing has to charge for heavy use (section 3)

slides.title: Customers put mobile reliability well ahead of AI, both when they leave and when they ask for features

claims.claim: Mobile reliability is the top reason accounts left in 2026; AI is the smallest named one
evidence: Main reason for churning, n = 1,190: Mobile app reliability 0.27; Price 0.22; Other 0.16; Missing integrations 0.15; Went out of business / sold 0.14; Switched for AI features 0.06

claims.claim: Twice as many customers rank a reliable mobile app first as rank AI scheduling first
evidence: 2x
Top-ranked feature request: Reliable technician mobile app 0.38; AI scheduling 0.19

claims.claim: The Head of Customer Success is right on the evidence: mobile reliability is cited 4.5 times as often as AI by accounts that left

slides.title: Even if AI caused the whole fall in win rate against Routewise, it costs about $0.6M of ARR a year

claims.claim: AI can explain at most part of the drop
evidence: Win rate in Routewise deals: Q1–Q2 2026 0.44; Q3 2026 0.37
Q3 2026: Routewise launched AI in its Pro plan and offered 20% off the first year in the same quarter
Loss notes: 31% mention AI, but a mention is not the cause, and the notes cover all losses, not only Routewise

claims.claim: $0.6M new ARR a year at most, if Copilot won back the whole fall
evidence: 1,560 deals a year with Routewise (60% of 2,600) × 7 pp lower win rate since Q1–Q2 2026 × $5,877.6 ARR per new 6.2-seat Core account = $0.6M new ARR a year, an upper bound

claims.claim: Sales memo: a third of deals lost to Routewise is about 328 deals, $1.9M a year, 3.0 times what the whole drop is worth

slides.title: Each quarter the mobile rewrite slips puts nearly twice as much ARR at risk as a quarter's wait for Copilot

claims.claim: 1.9x as much ARR at risk from delaying the rewrite as from waiting on Copilot
evidence: $544.3K ARR lost per quarter the rewrite slips: 27% of the 1,372 accounts that churn a year cite mobile, at $5,877.60 ARR each
$281.4K ARR lost per quarter Copilot waits: Routewise deals ($160K) plus accounts that switch for AI ($121K)
Churn reasons from 2026 churned accounts (n = 1,190); win rates from §7 of the briefing pack; live formulas in the Calculations sheet

claims.claim: Both sides are upper bounds; mobile first holds while the rewrite removes at least 52% of mobile churn
evidence: Mobile side: the rewrite ends mobile-reliability churn when it ships; neither side is proven to be the cause
Copilot side: Copilot wins back the whole Q3 drop and every AI-driven switch, although Routewise also cut prices by 20%
Pro is shifted, not lost, but waiting gives up about $257K of Pro contribution per quarter, one-off
On the 1,190 churned accounts that gave a reason, mobile risk is $472K a quarter, still 1.8 times

slides.title: How to package and price it
A flat $149 add-on draws heavy users: buyers cost $61.20 a month to serve and the top tenth $130.50

claims.claim: A flat price loses margin exactly where demand is
evidence: Inference cost per account, $ a month at $0.009 per request: Beta median (1,900 requests) 17.1; Beta mean (3,600) 32.4; Paywall buyers (6,800) 61.2; Top 10% of beta (14,500) 130.5
Add-on price $149.00
Buyers: use almost twice the beta mean
Top 10%: send 58% of requests at a flat fee
Add-on margin after inference, paywall buyers 58.9% ($149 − $61.20) ÷ $149
Add-on margin after inference, top 10% 12.4% ($149 − $130.50) ÷ $149
Request volumes from the 12-week beta; inference price fixed under the current contract through December 2027

slides.title: A Pro plan fits Brightwork's goals better than an add-on, with half the entry price and revenue that grows with seats

claims.claim: Pro costs half the add-on
evidence: Price for an average 6.2-seat account, a month: $149 add-on $149; Pro plan $74.4

claims.claim: Pro has the stronger precedent
evidence: Add-on: 14% of beta volunteers paid in the paywall test; Pro: 33% of accounts moved to the last new tier (2023) within a year

claims.claim: Pro charges for cost
evidence: Add-on: Nobody: heavy and light users pay the same flat fee; Pro: Per-seat fee plus an allowance, with overage above it

claims.claim: Pro removes a price gap in deals
evidence: Add-on: Priced on top of Core, against a rival that includes AI; Pro: Same packaging as Routewise's Pro plan since September 2026
Routewise launched AI scheduling included in its Pro plan in September 2026

claims.claim: Per-seat pricing turns seat growth into expansion revenue, the lever 105% NRR needs
evidence: Add-on: Flat per account; no gain as seats grow; Pro: Rises with every seat an account adds

slides.title: If a third of accounts move up as in 2023, Pro adds $2.9M of ARR, or $1.0M a year after costs

claims.claim: Pro adds $2.9M of ARR, or $1.0M a year after costs
evidence: $2.9M new ARR: 3,234 accounts (33% of 9,800) at $892.80 a year ($12 × 6.2 seats × 12)
− $1.3M inference: 3,600 requests a month per account (beta mean) at $0.009
− $0.6M platform, evaluation and support a year
= $1.03M contribution a year, before the one-off build

claims.claim: Pro beats the add-on and covers the NRR target, if at least 26% of accounts move
evidence: Add-on, same maths at the 14% paywall rate: $2.45M of ARR, $0.84M a year after costs
NRR: $2.89M is 5.0 percentage points of today's $57.6M ARR; the 4 percentage point gap needs $2.30M
At 14% (the rate measured at $149, twice Pro's price), Pro adds $1.22M and only $0.09M after costs; at 46%, $4.02M
Build: $1.47M (14 engineers for two quarters at $210K a year), repaid in about 17 months

claims.claim: Pro lifts NRR once, in the year accounts move up; lower mobile churn is what holds 105% after that

slides.title: Company margin stays above its floor only if Pro caps included usage near 5,300 requests per account a month

claims.claim: Pro needs a usage allowance to stay above the 75% floor
evidence: Inference cost per account, $ a month: Beta median (1,900 requests) 17.1; Beta mean (3,600) 32.4; Paywall buyers (6,800) 61.2; Top 10% of beta (14,500) 130.5
Pro revenue per account $74.40
Company margin, Pro at paywall-buyer usage 74.1%, same, with $2.38M of inference
Requests per account a month at a 75% margin 5,296 = (25% × $60.49M − $12.67M − $0.6M) ÷ (3,234 × $0.009 × 12)
Base case: 33% of accounts on Pro; platform cost counted as cost of revenue; company margin 78% today

claims.claim: Heavy users: move first; the top tenth costs more than Pro earns
Allowance: 854 requests per seat a month, overage above it
Inference at $0.009 per request is fixed through December 2027; the 35% fall in list prices over 12 months is upside from 2028 only

slides.title: Four gates tell the executive team early whether the plan stays on course

claims.claim: Gate 1: Pro migration keeps pace with the retention target
evidence: 26.3% of accounts on Pro within 12 months of launch

claims.claim: Gate 2: Usage stays inside the allowance that protects margin
evidence: 5,296 requests per Pro account a month, on average

claims.claim: Gate 3: January check: the rewrite targets enough mobile churn to go first; if not, launch Pro in Q2
evidence: 51.7% of mobile-reliability churn removed after launch

claims.claim: Gate 4: Win rate against Routewise recovers once Pro includes AI
evidence: 44% win rate in Routewise deals, the Q1–Q2 2026 level

claims.claim: Decision today: approve Pro at $12 more per seat, and hold the Q2 launch unless the January check fails gate 3

normalized.recommendation: Ship the mobile rewrite first, then launch Copilot in Q4 2027 in a Pro plan at $12 more per seat with a usage allowance. Decision today: approve Pro at $12 more per seat, and hold the Q2 launch unless the January check fails gate 3.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: "Package Copilot in Pro at $12 more per seat, not a $149 add-on"; a flat price loses margin exactly where demand is (58.9% margin for paywall buyers, 12.4% for top 10%); nobody pays for heavy use; priced on top of Core against a rival that includes AI; no gain as seats grow; $2.45M of ARR, $0.84M a year after costs at the 14% paywall rate.

alternatives_considered.option: Pro plan at $12 more per seat with usage allowance
alternatives_considered.treatment: Chosen: half the add-on entry price, stronger precedent (33% moved to last new tier in 2023), charges for cost, matches Routewise packaging, rises with seats; $2.9M ARR, $1.0M a year after costs at 33% migration.

alternatives_considered.option: Launch Copilot first / before the mobile rewrite
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: each quarter the rewrite slips puts $544.3K of ARR at risk vs $281.4K for a quarter's wait for Copilot (1.9x); mobile first holds while the rewrite removes at least 52% of mobile churn.
Fallback: if the January check finds the rewrite cannot fix half of mobile churn (gate 3, 51.7%), launch Pro in Q2 instead.
